messages:
maria: quick question — we're seeing more cases where the central platform needs to act on behalf of a project (billing checks, alerting, reconciliations) but we don't want org-level api keys floating around. thinking about a delegation pattern.
lucy: do we mean full impersonation or just delegated scoped tokens? prefer scoped tokens with explicit allowed actions :+1:
ajay: +1 to scoped. my proposal: short-lived delegation JWTs issued by a token-broker service. claims: sub=service-id, act_as=project-service-actor, aud=target-service, scope=[routes], exp TTL small (5m-15m).
samir: audit & rotation are the tricky bits. if tokens are long-lived we lose rotation and key compromise blast radius. ephemeral tokens + refresh flow + broker audit log solves that. also store issuance events in audit-store.
maria: exact sketch: broker gets authenticated request from platform svc (mTLS or svc token), validates requester policy, mints ephemeral token bound to project_id + allowed route prefixes + max_qps.
lucy: example token claim shape (draft):
```
{
  "iss": "redwood-token-broker",
  "sub": "svc-platform-1",
  "act_as": "project:proj-17:alert-agent",
  "aud": "redwood-inference-runtime",
  "scope": ["/v1/generate","/v1/embeddings"],
  "nbf": 1610000000,
  "exp": 1610000300,
  "bind_fingerprint": "sha256:..."
}
```
bind_fingerprint = optional TLS client cert fingerprint to mitigate token reuse if exfiltrated.
deploy-bot: deploy: jwt-broker v1 rolled to staging :rocket:
ajay: edge cases: 3rd-party webhooks and long-running ops. webhooks can't always refresh a 5m token. maybe we allow a scoped long-lived 'webhook' credential with very limited surface + strict ingress checks.
maria: also RBAC mapping question: should roles be inherited org->project? i think implicit inheritance is dangerous — prefer explicit grants. org roles give org-wide admin, but not auto project admin unless explicitly granted.
samir: agree. rule: no implicit escalation. mapping APIs can make grants convenient but must create explicit project bindings.
lucy: one more: token binding to client cert or PKCE-like flow for services where we can. that prevents stolen bearer tokens from being replayed.
maria: threat model notes: if broker compromised, attacker can mint tokens — need HSM/KMS for signing, rate limits, IP allowlist, and strong audit+alerting on abnormal mint patterns.
ajay: action items: (1) short RFC with token-broker API + claim schema + audit events, (2) prototype act_as claim issuance & runtime enforcement (3) doc for webhook long-lived credential pattern + controls.
maria: i'll draft the RFC skeleton. ajay + samir will prototype. lucy can add enforcement hooks to runtime.
ajay: i'll own prototype, aim for a staging demo by EOW. :+1:
samir: i'll add audit schema and rotate plan to the RFC. :thinking:
lucy: sounds good. ping me when draft is up, i'll review enforcement checks.
maria: thanks all — this should help eliminate org-level key sprawl and improve observability. :rotating_light:
